location.elevation_note: Elevation as reported by NASA POWER for this location (model grid context), not a surveyed point elevation.
location.cell_note: Values represent the data-grid cell containing this point (0.5° lat × 0.625° lon (MERRA-2 grid)), not a station at this exact location.

primary.method: OLS on monthly anomalies, AR(1)-adjusted (Santer et al. 2000)

mann_kendall_unadjusted.method: Original Mann-Kendall (assumes independent values; shown for transparency)

seasonal_kendall.method: Seasonal Kendall (Hirsch et al. 1982) on raw monthly values

practical.explanation: Statistical significance says whether a trend is distinguishable from noise; it does not say whether the change is large. 'Total change' is the fitted slope times the record length. It is compared with the typical year-to-year variability (standard deviation of detrended annual means). Whether a change of this size matters depends on the application and is not judged automatically.

verdict.label: Statistically significant increase
verdict.explanation: Both the autocorrelation-adjusted OLS test (p < 0.001) and the modified Mann-Kendall test (p < 0.001) reject 'no trend' at the 5% level.

trend.summary: From 1981 to 2025, near-surface air temperature at this location increased by 0.352 °C per decade (95% CI 0.213 to 0.492; adjusted OLS on monthly anomalies). Verdict: Statistically significant increase. A statistical trend describes change in this dataset. It does not by itself identify the cause of the change.
trend.causality_note: A statistical trend describes change in this dataset. It does not by itself identify the cause of the change.

warnings: Values are for the reanalysis grid cell containing the point (about 50 km), not a station measurement at that exact location.
Reanalysis trends can include artefacts from changes in the assimilated observing system (Gelaro et al. 2017).
NASA POWER re-packages MERRA-2; comparing POWER with MERRA-2 is not an independent validation.

method.deseasonalization: Monthly anomalies: each value minus the mean of its calendar month over the selected period.
tests: Primary: OLS on monthly anomalies with AR(1) effective-sample-size adjustment (Santer et al. 2000): n_eff = n(1−r1)/(1+r1), t-test with n_eff−2 df, 95% CI.
Modified Mann-Kendall test with Hamed & Rao (1998) variance correction, on monthly anomalies; Theil–Sen slope with rank-based CI.
Seasonal Kendall test (Hirsch et al. 1982) on raw monthly values, as an independent check that needs no baseline.
Robustness: OLS and Mann-Kendall on annual means; adjusted OLS with the first/last 3 years removed.
method.verdict_rule: 'Statistically significant' only if the adjusted OLS test AND the modified Mann-Kendall test both give p < 0.05 with the same sign; 'methods disagree' if exactly one does; 'suggestive' if neither does but at least one has p < 0.10; otherwise 'not detected'. Requires ≥ 10 years, ≥ 80% valid months, no gap > 24 months and n_eff ≥ 10.
